angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,008,765 km at 160.07 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.2474 +/- 0.0270 mas (same row, RUWE 1.36): 160.07 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.45 +/- 0.1 solar radii from Barber et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of IRAS 04125+2902 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract): 1,008,765 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.7 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Barber et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of IRAS 04125+2902 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4080 +/- 95 K from Barber et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of IRAS 04125+2902 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barber et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of IRAS 04125+2902 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/iras-04125-2902.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.960, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of IRAS 04125+2902 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.33161, from Barber et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of IRAS 04125+2902 (pscomppars): age 0.0033 Gyr, from Barber et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of IRAS 04125+2902 (pscomppars): rotation period 11.31 d, from Barber et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract)
